Montreal Communique 


March 23, 1970 


For release at will 


YMCA BACK ALLEY PROGRAM 
GETS SUPPORT FROM SCHOOL 


Using last summer's back alley program as a springboard, the Montreal 
YMCA's International Branch has persuaded more than half the pupils in 
Edward VII School to voluntarily remain after classes. 

Instead of dawdling in the streets, or returning to homes where 
both parents may be working, some 350 children age 8-15, now stay on 
Mondays and Fridays to participate in supervised recreational activities. 

The school is located on Esplanade near Van Horne, in one of Montreal's 
so-called ‘grey areas' of under-employment and sub-standard housing. 

Such conditions, aggravated by a scarcity of recreational facilities, 
tend to foster delinquency, stifle initiative and minimize opportunities 
for self-development. 

The after-school project is designed to help break this cycle by 
filling a significant part of the leisure-time gap. 

The program was conccived and is run by the YMCA, in co-operation 
with school authorities. It includes gym and sports, arts and crafts, 
drama and club groups. 

Except for swimming, which is carried on in the Y's pool, all 
activities are on school premises, in a milieu well known to both 
the youngsters and their parents. 

This eliminates the need for any extra travel and relieves anxieties 
about venturing, unprepared into an environment which, though potentially 
rewarding, is also unfamiliar.
